name: Hanan
overview: Hanan was a male figure mentioned in the Bible who is noted for having a chamber in the Temple, as recorded in Jeremiah 35:4. There is no information about his tribal affiliation or additional personal details beyond this unique attribute. His presence in the scriptural text is brief but distinct due to this association with the Temple.
namesAndTitles: The name Hanan means 'gracious' in Hebrew, reflecting a proper name that was not given directly by God. This meaning may suggest a character trait or a hopeful attribute, though the text does not elaborate further.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Hanan explicitly as the son of Igdaliah, according to Jeremiah 35:4. No other family relationships are recorded beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Hanan's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his connection with the Temple, specifically having his own chamber there, which implies a position of some standing or responsibility. This detail situates him within the religious context of the time and highlights the importance of Temple service or residence. His mention alongside his father Igdaliah also points to a family involved in the religious life of Israel.
